author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
IPR014014 RNA helicase, DEAD-box type, Q motif

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel SoYb (Q9VL52)

* **Description of issue**
A claude review of SoYb GO annotations recommended removing its 'RNA helicase activity annotation. This comes from IPR014014. The review said:

“RNA helicase activity is assigned from the DEAD-box Q-motif InterPro signature and EC 3.6.4.13. SoYb has lost the Walker A lysine, the catalytic glutamate of the DEAD motif (DDYD), motif III and motif VI, so it is most likely a pseudo-helicase.    reason: An electronic inference contradicted by sequence. Every catalytic hallmark of a DEAD-box helicase is missing, and the alignment is cross-checked by the position of UniProt's own DEAD-box motif annotation. UniProt names the protein only a 'Putative' helicase. No biochemical data support activity.”


So, I don't think the presence of this site/motif alone is sufficient to be annotated with 'RNA helicase activity - may need to remove?
title: InterPro2GO issue: IPR014014 RNA helicase, DEAD-box type, Q motif InterPro entry

author: sarach06
